text: and i still cant figure out this whole grid system. first and foremost, is this grid doing the same grid the game is doing?

events.text: NOTE: req_0433's captured text is the GRID QUESTION; the zoom-fling fix (4da4364d2) cited above addressed the concurrent 'zoom shifts view up-left' report that arrived in the same exchange. Grid answer for the question itself: the iso build grid IS the game's grid — world-scale contract is 1 tile = 1 meter (WORLD_TUNING.defaultCellSizeMeters=1), the build-piece snap pitch is gridMeters=1 (snap.ts), and the iso visual grid draws a line every 1 tile (bold every 8). All three coincide, so pieces snap to the same cells the game and F2 use. Likely perceptual snag: grid LINES sit on cell EDGES (integers) while piece CENTERS sit on cell CENTERS (N+0.5), so a piece reads as half a cell off the lines; awaiting the user on what specifically is confusing before changing the visual.

resolution: Zooming flung the whole iso view up-left by a huge amount. Root cause: the onScroll event payload provides scrollX/scrollY/deltaX/deltaY but NO x/y, so local(e) read the cursor as (0,0) and zoomToCursor anchored on (-rect.x,-rect.y) — a far off-screen pixel for the bottom-right pane, whose ground-plane intersection lands way off the map, dragging centre with it. Fixed by reading the engine cursor via getMouseX/getMouseY (the authoritative source the placement-ghost poll already uses) and converting to pane-local coords, with a pane-centre fallback. Zoom now keeps the point under the pointer fixed in and out. Committed 4da4364d2, bundles clean.
